definitions.explanation: Happening without deliberate effort or external force; arising as a natural consequence.

examples.japanese: {練習|れんしゅう}を{続|つづ}ければ、おのずと{上達|じょうたつ}する。
examples.english: If you keep practicing, you'll naturally improve.

examples.japanese: {時間|じかん}が{経|た}てば、おのずと{答|こた}えは{見|み}えてくる。
examples.english: If you give it time, the answer will naturally become clear.

examples.japanese: おのずと{涙|なみだ}がこぼれた。

notes:
KANJI:
Can be written as {自|おの}ずと. The kanji {自|おの} emphasizes "self" or "by itself."

ALTERNATIVE FORMS:
・おのずから - slightly more formal/literary variant
・{自|おの}ずと - kanji spelling

USAGE:
Describes events or outcomes that occur without forcing:
・おのずと{結果|けっか}が{出|で}る (results will come naturally)
・おのずと{分|わ}かる (will naturally understand)
・おのずと{限界|げんかい}がある (there are natural limits)

NUANCE:
Implies a natural, organic process rather than forced or artificial one. Often suggests that patience or proper conditions will lead to a natural outcome.

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{自然|しぜん}と - naturally (more common in casual speech)
・ひとりでに - by itself, automatically
・いつの{間|ま}にか - before one knows it
